hints: Factor out the leading coefficient $4$ from the first two terms: $4(x^2 - 6x) + p$.
Complete the square inside the bracket: $x^2 - 6x = (x - 3)^2 - 9$.
Expand the outer factor and group the constant term: $4(x - 3)^2 - 36 + p$.
walkthrough:
Factor out $4$ from the terms involving $x$:
$$4x^2 - 24x + p = 4(x^2 - 6x) + p$$

Complete the square for the quadratic inside the parentheses:
$$x^2 - 6x = (x - 3)^2 - 3^2 = (x - 3)^2 - 9$$

Distribute $4$ and combine constant terms:
$$4\left((x - 3)^2 - 9\right) + p = 4(x - 3)^2 - 36 + p = 4(x - 3)^2 + (p - 36)$$
where $a = 4$, $b = -3$, and $c = p - 36$.

hints: From the completed square form $4(x-3)^2 + (p-36) = 0$, no real roots occur when the minimum value is strictly positive ($p - 36 > 0$).
Alternatively, use the discriminant condition for no real roots: $\Delta = b^2 - 4ac < 0$.
State the set of values of $p$ as an inequality: $p > 36$.
walkthrough:
Use the completed square form $4(x - 3)^2 + (p - 36) = 0$:
$$4(x - 3)^2 = 36 - p$$

Since $(x - 3)^2 \ge 0$ for all real $x$, there are no real roots when the right-hand side is strictly negative (or equivalently, the minimum value is positive):
$$p - 36 > 0 \implies p > 36$$
